answer: Cross-epoch trajectory matching. Each identity hashes its action sequence per epoch into a chained digest; verifiers require the new epoch's first actions to continue the prior digest's trajectory within a tolerance band. A duplicate identity spawned fresh cannot inherit the history, so it must replay an old trajectory under a haven of time constraints, and mismatches flag divergence. An attacker sustaining N clones across epochs pays N distinct behavioral histories, plus the ivory cost of maintaining coherent action traces, roughly linear per identity.
